briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. We will now begin the climate briefing for September 26, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Intensifying Climate Crisis Phenomena and Infrastructure Threats
sections.content: Direct threats from climate change are rapidly increasing both domestically and internationally. Domestically, the vulnerability of national infrastructure is being exposed, with extreme heat degrading aircraft performance [1] and concerns raised about the risk of flooding at military airports and bases [2]. Internationally, the major floods in Nepal have been referred to as a 'global warning' about climate change, prompting calls for international aid [5, 32, 42], and in Alaska, unpredictable changes are being observed, such as melting glaciers, collapsing mountains, and rivers turning orange [21, 38]. The Earth's most vulnerable regions are bearing the brunt of climate change, with Antarctic sea ice reaching its lowest level on satellite record and Papua's 'eternal snow' facing the threat of disappearance [47, 50]. UN leaders have emphasized that the climate crisis is no longer a 'distant warning' [28], reminding us that extreme weather events such as heatwaves, wildfires, hurricanes, and floods are severely impacting daily life [40].

sections.title: ⚠️ Impacts on Ecosystems and Economic Activities
sections.content: Climate change is having widespread and uneven impacts on global ecosystems and key economic activities. According to research, climate change is expected to unevenly reshape Somalia's fisheries [26], and the habitats of European bumblebees have already been confirmed to be undergoing reorganization [35]. Indonesia's coffee trade is shrinking, directly hit by climate change [36], and changes due to climate change are also being detected in wine production in mountainous regions at the Trentodoc festival [43]. These changes are also affecting productivity [34], and their ripple effects are expanding, with the UK, the European Union, and Kenya classifying climate change as a threat to international security [46].

sections.title: 🌱 Domestic Carbon Neutrality and Renewable Energy Transition Efforts
sections.content: Domestically, diverse efforts are underway to respond to climate change and achieve carbon neutrality goals. Local governments' efforts to encourage citizen participation and practical action are prominent, with Yongin Special City offering benefits to participants in its carbon neutrality points for vehicles program [7, 9, 11], and Gwangyang City receiving the top award for its carbon neutrality implementation administration [10]. The Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy has set a target of 30.2% for renewable energy generation by 2030 [14], and carbon reduction efforts are active in both the private and public sectors, including Konecranes' goal to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 90% [6] and Jeju public institutions' use of renewable energy for Samdasoo water production [16]. The market outlook for transformers and inverters for battery storage, which will drive the growth of renewable energy grid connection [17, 18], is interpreted as a positive sign for the expansion of domestic renewable energy infrastructure. However, the surging electricity demand from the AI and semiconductor industries is emerging as a new challenge for achieving carbon neutrality goals [8], requiring continuous efforts for efficient energy management and renewable energy expansion.

sections.title: 🌍 International Community's Calls for Climate Action and Research Trends
sections.content: The international community recognizes the importance of responding to climate change and is urging action and conducting research at various levels. Al Gore stated that 2026 could be a turning point for climate action [20], but also raised questions about whether it can be addressed in time [44]. The '2026 Global Carbon Neutrality Report' is scheduled to be released at the Tsinghua University Forum [12], and scientific understanding and adaptation efforts regarding climate change are ongoing, with Burlington County selected as a new climate change research institution and crop cultivability research for climate change response being conducted in the UK [4, 24]. The oil price shock in the wake of the Iran war is accelerating the major renewable energy transition in Southeast Asia [13], and renewable energy investments are actively taking place worldwide, including the completion of a 100MW solar project in Zambia [19]. Furthermore, the role of media is also being highlighted as important, with EBS covering the impacts on the Himalayan region through a special documentary on climate change [3].

briefing.closing: As discussed in today's briefing, the climate crisis is having severe global impacts, and domestic and international response efforts must be continuously strengthened. This concludes today's climate briefing.

summary.phenomenon: The Hawaiian Islands have recently experienced three significant tropical storms: Hurricane Lala in August, Lowell in early September, and Nolo, which intensified into a hurricane on Thursday night. summary.cause: Rising ocean temperatures are fueling more severe weather, and an intensified El Niño phenomenon is making Hawaii a target for an increased number of storms.
summary.outlook: Hurricane Nolo is anticipated to bring heavy rainfall and high surf to the Hawaiian Islands.
